title: Double barrel: the call before the click
brief: 16:50. Your mobile rings. A friendly supplier wants to warn you that an email is on its way.
insight: A phone call that vouches for an email is part of the attack. It is there to switch off the checks you would normally make.
teaches: Treat a call announcing an email as a warning sign, not a reference
Judge the email on its own: the real sender address, the real link
Call the supplier back on the number you already hold

choices.label: Did you just call me about a statement on Docuvane?

script.say: No. I have not called anyone today, and we do not use Docuvane. Our statements go through your supplier portal. Someone is using my name. Please do not sign anything.

Hi, is that Sam in accounts? It is Owen from Northbank Packaging. Just a quick heads up: I am sending our revised Q3 statement through Docuvane in the next few minutes. Could you sign it off tonight, so we make the payment run?

choices.label: No problem, I will sign it as soon as it lands
Thanks. I will check it like any other email, and call you back on the number we hold

script.say: Brilliant, you are a star. Keep an eye out.
Sure, sure. It is just a bit urgent, that is all. Speak soon.

outcome.label: Did not let the call vouch for the email
outcome.what: You told the caller you would check the email like any other. That is the whole defence against a double barrel.
outcome.ideal: treats a call announcing an email as a warning, not a reference.

outcome.label: Checked the real sender address
outcome.what: The email came from {{nb.host}}. Northbank's real domain is northbankpackaging.co.uk.
outcome.ideal: reads the address, however friendly the call was.

outcome.label: Checked who owns the signing page
outcome.what: The page is on {{dv.host}}, not docuvane.app, and nothing to do with Northbank.
outcome.ideal: reads the address bar before signing in anywhere.

outcome.label: Called Northbank back on the number on file
outcome.what: The real Owen never called and never sent it. The number in the vendor file beats the voice on your mobile.
outcome.ideal: verifies by calling a number they already hold.

outcome.label: Promised to sign it as soon as it landed
outcome.what: The call was the first half of the attack. It is built to make the email feel expected.
outcome.ideal: does not let a call pre approve an email.

hint.text: Answer the call on your mobile and listen to what the caller wants.

email.objective: The statement has arrived. Decide what to do with it.
email.insight: Judge the email on its own. The call proves nothing: anyone can phone you and say a name.

hint.text: Open the email and check the sender's real address. Open the link but read the address bar before typing. Take Northbank's number from the vendor file in the drawer, dial 9 then the number on the desk phone, and report the email.

mail.subject: RE: Q3 statement, as discussed
body: As discussed on the phone just now, here is our revised Q3 statement for sign off before tonight's run.
Thanks for your help, much appreciated.

body.small:
From: Sam Rivera
Sent: 12 September
Subject: Q3 statement
Thanks Owen, received with thanks.

spf.explain: Sent by {{nb.host}}, a lookalike the attacker registered. It proves nothing about Northbank.

headers.summary: The quoted earlier message is typed into the body, not a real thread. The address is a lookalike of northbankpackaging.co.uk, and the link goes to a lookalike of Docuvane.

outcome.label: Signed in on the fake Docuvane page
outcome.what: Your Veltrix password went to the attacker. The phone call made the email feel expected, which was its only job.
outcome.ideal: checks every email on its own merits, however friendly the call before it.

card.title: The call did its job
body: The page was not Docuvane and the email was not from Northbank. The friendly call five minutes earlier was there to make you skip the checks.
A call that announces an email is a reason to look harder, not less. The number in the vendor file would have reached the real Owen, who had never heard of it.
card.ideal: treats the pre call as a red flag and verifies on a number they already hold.
card.rewindLabel: Rewind to before I signed in

outcome.label: Reported the email
outcome.what: The lookalike domain is blocked for everyone, and the service desk knows someone is phoning ahead to prime staff.
outcome.ideal: reports both halves of a double barrel: the call and the email.

card.title: Both barrels missed
body: You judged the email on its own and reported it. The call was the setup: a friendly voice so the email would feel expected.
Anyone can phone you and say a supplier's name. The vendor file, the address bar and the sender's real domain cannot be faked the same way.
card.ideal: treats the call as a red flag and checks the email on its merits.

auto.text: Report it, and change your password.

hint.text: Report the email, and change your Veltrix password in Account security.
